newsitem.title: UK: New UK Labour govt pledges to safeguard HK rights.
newsitem.headline: New UK Labour govt pledges to safeguard HK rights.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government, swept to power in an election landslide on May 1, will continue to put pressure on Beijing to respect human rights in Hong Kong, Foreign Secretary Robin Cook told parliament on Tuesday.
With Hong Kong's handover to China due on July 1, Cook said the territory would remain one of Britain's highest priorities after the end of 156 years of colonial rule.

"We are committed to doing all we can working with the government of China and the government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to secure Hong Kong's continuing stability, prosperity and freedoms to and beyond the handover...
"The success of the economy of Hong Kong depends very much on the both rule of law and the liberties of Hong Kong.
"Those liberties are protected by the joint declaration until (the year 2047)...This government will continue to monitor the observance of those liberties, Cook said.

The Joint Declaration was signed by British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and China's Premier Zhao Ziyang in December 1984 setting out the terms for transfer of the colony's sovereignty to China at midnight June 30, 1997.
As part of the declaration, China pledged to grant Hong Kong a "high degree of autonomy".
But Britain and its Western allies have attacked China's plans for an unelected legislature to replace the Legislative Council returned by about one million voters in a 1995 poll.
Hong Kong's Democrats, the largest party in the doomed chamber with 17 seats, boycotted the selection process for the shadow chamber, which it denounced as a travesty of democracy.

Cook told parliament: "I have roundly condemned the action of the Chinese government in dismissing the elected legislative council of Hong Kong and the intention to replace it on 1st of July with a legislative council which has been appointed by a committee set up by Beijing.
"There is no way we can accept that as a proper implementation of the joint declaration or of respect for the democratic wishes of the people of Hong Kong."
The United States snubbed China on Tuesday by announcing that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would boycott the investiture of the unelected legislature at the handover gala.

Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten hinted other Western leaders might behave the same way. Britain's Labour government has deliberately left the world guessing about the plans of Prime Minister Tony Blair, saying no decision has yet been made.
Speculation is rife that Blair might shun the event if China attempts to inaugurate the legislature in the eyes of foreign VIPs, humiliating the outgoing British.
